title: Install | repo-revamp
description: Install repo-revamp in Claude Code with one marketplace command or two steps, check the requirements, and know what a working install looks like.
lead: One command, or two if you prefer to add the marketplace first. Nothing is installed globally and no configuration file is edited by hand.

sections.text: The one-line install

sections.caption: The four steps from zero to a first revamp.
sections.text_alt: Step one: add the marketplace with the plugin marketplace add command, passing FiredMosquito831/repo-revamp. Step two: install the plugin with the plugin install command, either by name at danube-labs or in one line with the marketplace flag. Step three: restart Claude Code so the skill, commands and agents load in a new session. Step four: run the revamp command on a repository, which starts the state machine at INTAKE.

sections.text: The repository is its own marketplace, so one command installs the plugin and registers the marketplace it comes from:

sections.label: Claude Code
sections.text: /plugin install repo-revamp --marketplace FiredMosquito831/repo-revamp
Run it inside Claude Code. The plugin is fetched from the public repository, and the five commands and three agents become available in the session.
The marketplace route
If you want the marketplace registered on its own, add it first and install from it by name:

sections.label: Claude Code
sections.text:
/plugin marketplace add FiredMosquito831/repo-revamp
/plugin install repo-revamp@danube-labs
The marketplace is called `danube-labs`. It lists one plugin, `repo-revamp`, whose source is the repository root.
From a local clone, point the marketplace at the checkout instead of the repository name:

sections.label: Claude Code
sections.text:
/plugin marketplace add /absolute/path/to/repo-revamp
/plugin install repo-revamp@danube-labs
Requirements

sections.caption: What the plugin needs, and what each piece is for
head: Requirement
Why
rows: Loads the skill, the commands and the agents.
The revamp works in a worktree and commits to a branch.
The GitHub steps: pull requests, Pages, repository metadata.
Runs the builder and the three plugin scripts.
Pillow and imagehash, in a scratch environment
Only for perceptual clustering and contact sheets. The inventory and SHA-256 de-duplication use the standard library.

sections.text: Nothing else is required. The builder needs Jinja2 and MarkupSafe, pinned in the site's own requirements file; the plugin's install does not add them to any product manifest.
What a working install looks like

The plugin validates itself before anything is published. The capture below is the real output of `claude plugin validate . --strict` in a checkout of this repository. Paths are replaced with `<repo>`; the text is otherwise exact.
A second check runs the repository's own validator and prints one line per component. It is the check the CI workflow runs on every push.
After a restart, `claude plugin details repo-revamp` should list the six skills, the three agents and no hooks, MCP servers or LSP servers.
What "installed" means

After a restart the plugin contributes four things to a session: the `repo-revamp` skill, which is model-invocable, so saying "revamp this repo" loads it; five slash commands under the `repo-revamp` prefix; three subagents that the skill can delegate to; and the working files the playbook writes outside the repository. It adds no hooks, no MCP servers and no LSP servers.

The skill is the contract and the state machine. The commands are entry points into it. The agents are the delegated workers. Nothing runs until you ask for a revamp, and nothing in your repositories changes until a revamp command starts.
Update and uninstall
Updates come from the marketplace. Refresh the marketplace and reinstall the plugin; the version in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` is the only place the version is declared.

sections.label: Claude Code
sections.text:
/plugin marketplace update danube-labs
/plugin update repo-revamp@danube-labs
To remove it, uninstall the plugin and, if you added it only for this, remove the marketplace:

sections.label: Claude Code
sections.text:
/plugin uninstall repo-revamp@danube-labs
/plugin marketplace remove danube-labs

sections.title: The plugin does not touch your repositories
sections.text: Installing it adds a skill, five commands and three agents to Claude Code. It does not clone, edit or configure any repository until you run a revamp command on one.
Next

claims.claim: The repository is its own marketplace.
The one-line install is /plugin install repo-revamp --marketplace FiredMosquito831/repo-revamp.
The marketplace route is /plugin marketplace add FiredMosquito831/repo-revamp then /plugin install repo-revamp@danube-labs.
The marketplace is named danube-labs and lists one plugin.
The plugin's source is the repository root.
A local clone can be registered as a marketplace by absolute path.
The requirements are Claude Code with plugin support, git, gh and Python 3.12.
Pillow and imagehash are needed only for clustering and contact sheets.
The builder needs Jinja2 and MarkupSafe, pinned in requirements-site.txt.
claude plugin validate . --strict passes on this repository.
The repository validator prints one PASS line per component and runs in CI.
The installed plugin lists six skills, three agents and no hooks, MCP servers or LSP servers.
The plugin version is declared only in .claude-plugin/plugin.json.
